analyst_view.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 points) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 points) under pressure from their own fans after more than a month without a home win; the players have vowed to win at El Molinón. Nicolás Larcamón has up to eight absences: Juan Otero and Àlex Corredera are banned (Corredera's appeal was rejected) and Sarco is unlikely, which the numbers count, but Antonio Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad are also injured and are not in the numbers, leaving the attack very thin with academy players called on. Las Palmas, improving under new coach Albert Sánchez, are without Opoku (banned) and several injured players the numbers know about, plus Ale García (knocks), who is not in them; Viti and Sergio Ruiz are close but not ready. LaLiga's match page now lists Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo first among the officials, so he looks set to referee; the numbers had no referee for this game, and his Segunda record in our data is a little above the league's card average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already cut Sporting for Otero, Corredera and Sarco. I lean lower to about 2.1 because Sporting are also without forward Antonio Casas, Gelabert and Pablo García, so the attack rests on academy players and a barely fit Andrés Ferrari, and Las Palmas lose Ale García as well.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, close to both sides' recent levels. Sporting will push for a home win their fans demand, but with a weakened attack that does not clearly add corners, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, raised for both sides' recent cards (21 each in their last six) and trimmed for two past meetings, but with no referee in them. LaLiga's page lists Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo, who has averaged about 5.8 cards in 40 Segunda games in our data against a league average of 5.3, so I add a little to about 5.4; Sporting's recent red cards and the tense home mood are already in the momentum figures.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, with a boost for Sporting's 86 shots in their last six. That form came with players now injured (Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García) on top of the counted absences, so I trim it to about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. With Sporting's main forwards out and Las Palmas missing Ale García too, I lower it to about 7.9.
